.👈 Effective Centers
(Introduction to the book 'Effectiveness in an Ineffective Institutional Environment')
Everyone is looking for big deeds; deeds of the revolutionary kind; hoping to fix the world quickly and all at once. The government is either pursuing a global revolution and overthrowing arrogance, through organizing resistance forces; or it is pursuing writing a vision plan that will become first in everything in the region within a short time. The government's opponents and critics are also seeking to overthrow the government by organizing widespread protests to fix the country overnight and with a revolution. But wars' main achievement has been blood, tyranny, and displacement, and revolutions' main achievement has been the destruction of the institutional and physical infrastructure of society and the postponement of democracy and development for several generations. The reality is this: the world has been improved and advanced by micro-level individual efforts and medium-scale collective actions.

entry.summary:
Source: @Renani_Mohsen

.👈 The Revolutionary City (Book Introduction)
We still have an old and traditional understanding of revolution. The nature of 21st-century revolutions is completely different from those of previous centuries. Urbanization, information technology, and globalization have changed the nature and dynamics of revolutionary movements. In the book 'The Revolutionary City,' Mark Baisinger, by analyzing historical developments and examining recent examples of revolutions, provides a theoretical framework for analyzing urban civil revolutions in the new era. The content and main theory of the book can be summarized in two points. One is the 'spatial theory of revolution' and the other is 'the power of numbers' instead of the power of weapons. entry.title: .👈 Personal Geography (Book Introduction) Dr. Morteza Nemati, the resigned…
entry.summary:
Source: @Renani_Mohsen

.👈 Personal Geography (Book Introduction)
Dr. Morteza Nemati, the resigned professor of Shahid Chamran University of Ahvaz, is one of my staunchest critics in cyberspace. He believes that the methods of people like me, which are based on dialogue and understanding, with the aim of gradual and low-cost transformation of the existing situation, are not only fruitless in today's Iran but also reinforce oppressive structures. See one of his critiques here:
https://t.me/MortezaNemati1/233
In December 2023, he tore up his doctoral degree, which he had received from the University of Tehran in 2010, in front of the camera in protest against the University of Tehran granting an honorary doctorate to Bashar al-Assad. Watch the video of this symbolic act of his at the following link:
https://t.me/MortezaNemati1/115
A year before that, after twelve years of teaching at Shahid Chamran University of Ahvaz, he had resigned from the faculty of that university in protest against the unscientific, non-transparent, and discriminatory processes in the selection and promotion of faculty members. Over these years, to earn an honorable living, he started a restaurant, painted, baked bread, and did many other things; and now he is setting up a small rock climbing school for teenagers in his hometown (Abdanan).
Now he has written his experience of these years of pressure, discrimination, loneliness, and hardship, in the university and in society, in a book titled 'Personal Geography.' His book has not been granted a publication permit, and he has now shared it with us digitally. His pen is biting, his language is blunt, his criticism is fearless, and sometimes borders on insult. But I believe in the words of John Maynard Keynes: 'Words ought to be a little wild, for they are the assaults of thoughts on the unthinking.' Read the book 'Personal Geography' at the following link:
https://t.me/Renani_Mohsen/728

entry.title: .👈 How Can a Country Be Stolen? (Book Introduction 👆👆👆) This book,…
entry.summary:
Source: @Renani_Mohsen

.👈 How Can a Country Be Stolen? (Book Introduction 👆👆👆)
This book, after remaining in the publication queue for two years without receiving a permit, was finally published digitally by the author. The book provides good information, history, and analysis of the processes and consequences of privatization throughout the entire post-revolutionary period. By reading this book, we understand why privatization in Iran did not lead to the formation of a competitive and dynamic economy and only resulted in the formation of a 'new class' of rentier capitalists. In my opinion, the Islamic Republic, through crony privatization, first became an economic fiefdom, and then the new class that emerged from economic fiefdom also moved the political structure of governance towards political fiefdom. Now Iran's economy and politics have become various fiefdoms in the hands of specific political-economic groups. The experience of Russia and some other countries also shows that these fiefdoms turn into economic and political gangsterism during long-term political-economic instabilities and crises.
Reading this book can be useful for those interested in understanding the causes of today's stagnation of Iran's economy.

entry.summary:
Source: @Renani_Mohsen

.👈 Animation and Sexual Life
About five years ago, I participated in the 'Sexual Wisdom' series and spoke about 'Development and Sexual Life.' Because I believed that irrational taboos must be broken and the way must be opened for collective rationality. That series, without the support of official institutions, was a successful series and brought important topics to families. See my interview with that series here:
https://www.aparat.com/v/LV4U5
Now, after five years, a new season of that series titled 'Animation and Sexual Life' has been produced, which can provide important awareness to families who have children and where animation takes up a large part of their children's time. Caring for the data that unconsciously enters our children's minds in the process of daily life is a great responsibility on the shoulders of parents. The images that are imprinted on a child's mind in childhood through watching films and animations gradually create archetypes that cast a shadow over the person's mind and language for the rest of their life. A large part of our children's time passes in front of screens without any screening, and this is the most important gateway for harm to children. Watching and listening to the 'Animation and Sexual Life' series can make parents sensitive to the choice of films and animations that children watch.
This series deserves promotion because it has not only not been supported by official cultural institutions, but has even been denied an official publication permit due to the narrow-mindedness resulting from patriarchal cultural sediments. Therefore, it is fitting that affluent people attached to development support such productions.
Watch this series at the following link:
https://www.youtube.com/@kheradjensi

📺 Release of Dr. Mohsen Renani's Development Lectures
🎙Instructor: Mohsen Renani

🔸 What initiates a society's movement towards the ladder of development, and what provides the energy needed to climb the difficult steps of this ladder, is nothing but the 'common understanding' and 'common demand' of the people for development.
🔸 Everything begins with 'wanting,' and it is impossible for people to want a common goal and not achieve it, and it is impossible for any government, no matter how powerful, to have enough energy to oppose the common will of the people.
🔸 In these days when the air pollution of many cities in the country takes our breath away, and the heaviness of lead tightens our chests, we want to open our minds and fly in the clear and beautiful sky of development. 🔸 'Development Lectures' is a novel and structured video series that aims to explain the concept of development to all Iranian development-seekers.
